plugins.name: law-student
plugins.description: Drills Socratically, briefs cases, builds outlines, runs bar prep sessions tuned to your jurisdiction, grades IRAC practice, and plans the study schedule — without ever writing it for you.

skills.name: bar-prep-questions
skills.description: Bar prep questions — MBE or essay, targeted at your weak subjects and bar jurisdiction. Tracks misses and comes back to patterns. Use when the user says "bar prep", "MBE questions", "practice essay", or "test me for the bar".
headings: Exam type — ask first, do not assume
When unsure of the jurisdiction's rule

skills.name: case-brief
skills.description: Brief a case in your preferred format. In drill-me mode, makes the student state the holding first. Use when the user says "brief [case]", "what's the holding in", "case brief", or pastes a case.
headings: The "don't brief it for me" rule (hard rule)
The brief — scaffold, then the student fills
What this skill does not do

skills.name: cold-call-prep
skills.description: Prep for a cold-call — predict the professor's likely questions and drill them Socratically, flagging where you're shaky so you know what to re-read before class. Use when the user says "prep for class tomorrow", "cold call [case]", "what might [professor] ask on", or points at assigned reading.
headings: Questions likely to come up in class:
What this skill does not do

skills.name: cold-start-interview
skills.description: About-you interview and materials intake — classes, bar jurisdiction, learning style (drill-me vs explain-to-me), past outlines, graded essays, old exams, MBE sets, syllabi, papers. Use on a fresh install, when the user says "set up" or "get started", or with --check-integrations to re-probe connectors.
headings: Check for the shared company profile
After the user picks quick or full
Quick start or full setup — branching
Part 0: Who's using this, and what's connected
Part 2: How you learn (the key question) (2 min)
Part 3: Where you're strong and weak (1 min)
Part 4: Materials (3-5 min) — this is where the seed docs live

skills.name: customize
skills.description: Guided customization of your law-student study profile — change one thing without re-running the whole cold-start interview. Adjust current classes, learning style, outline preferences, bar prep subjects, seed materials, or study session cadence. Use when the user says "change my [thing]", "add a class", "update my profile", "new semester", or "customize".

skills.name: exam-forecast
skills.description: Analyze past exams from the same professor to surface patterns — subject weighting, recurring issue-spot traps, favored hypo types, policy-vs-doctrine mix — and forecast likely emphases for the upcoming exam. Use when the user says "what's on the exam", "analyze past exams", "predict the exam", or shares past exams.
headings: Step 4: Forecast for the upcoming exam
Topics covered this semester but rarely tested

skills.name: flashcards
skills.description: Generate or drill flashcards for black-letter memorization — Leitner-style buckets, per-subject markdown storage, drill mode with self-assessment. Use when the user says "drill flashcards", "make flashcards from", "quiz me on cards", or wants to memorize rules.
headings: What this skill does not do

skills.name: irac-practice
skills.description: Grade an IRAC essay for structure, issue-spotting, rule accuracy, analysis depth, and organization. Does NOT rewrite the essay or show a model answer; tracks patterns across sessions. Use when the user says "grade my IRAC", "check my essay", or "I wrote this, give me feedback".
headings: Writing sample — labeled example only (do not copy)

skills.name: legal-writing
skills.description: Structural feedback on a legal writing draft (memo, brief, paper, exam essay) — organization, analysis depth, clarity, citation form. NEVER rewrites the draft. Use when the user says "feedback on my memo", "read my draft", or "critique my brief".
headings: One example to illustrate — do not copy
Step 4: If the student asks you to rewrite

skills.name: outline-builder
skills.description: Build or extend a course outline in your format, from class notes and casebook. Scaffolds — it does not write the outline for you. Use when the user says "outline [subject]", "add to my outline", "build an outline from", or points at class materials.
headings: The "don't write it for me" rule (hard rule)
Step 3: Build — scaffold first, content from sources
What this skill does not do

skills.name: session
skills.description: Run a focused N-question study session on a subject — MBE, essay, or flashcards. Tracks performance and updates the study plan. Use when the user says "run me 10 questions on [subject]", "do a session on [subject]", "let's do 5 cards on [subject]", or wants to drill a fixed number of questions and have the plan adapt.

skills.name: socratic-drill
skills.description: Socratic drilling — it asks, you answer, it pushes back. Does NOT give you the answer until you've earned it. Use when the user says "drill me on", "quiz me", "socratic", "test me on [subject]", or wants to study actively.
headings: Step 4: Only after they get there
What this skill does not do

skills.name: study-plan
skills.description: Build or update a long-term bar prep (or exam prep) study plan — phases, subjects weighted by weakness, daily session schedule, adaptive to session history in study-plan.yaml. Use when the user says "build a study plan", "plan my bar prep", "schedule my studying", or "how should I study for [X]".
headings: Step 1: What are we planning for
Step 2: Inputs — one at a time, wait for each
What this skill does not do
